findings.description: The one-line fallback `REVIEW_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT="$(cat "$REVIEW_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"` is copy-pasted twice per file (post step and metrics step), on top of the existing template/repo-copy mirroring already guarded by test/workflow-sync.test.ts. This intra-file duplication (4 sites total) isn't test-covered, so a future semantic change to the fallback means editing four sites by hand. Given GitHub Actions has no native shared-snippet primitive short of a composite action, this is a defensible tradeoff rather than a regression.

The `run:` steps moved from a single clear line to a `run: |` block where `VAR="$(...)" \` is a continuation into the next line's command. This scoping is correct today, but a future edit that inserts a line between the assignment and the command, or drops the trailing backslash, silently drops the env var with no error — it would just fall back to the older-agent-init code path at runtime. The file already uses backslash-continued multi-line shell elsewhere (e.g. a `gh api -X PUT ... \` line), so the idiom isn't foreign, which keeps this a nit rather than a real regression risk.
